story: Before he was a sage, Valmiki was a robber called Ratnakara. When Narada asked whether his family would share his sins, they refused, and he sat in meditation for so long that an anthill (valmika) grew over him. He went on to write the Ramayana and gave Sita shelter in his hermitage.
belief: He is honoured as the Adi Kavi, the first poet, and as guru by the Valmiki community. Valmiki Jayanti celebrates his birth.
turns: His past as a robber is the whole point of his story: no one is beyond change. In one version he could at first only chant 'mara', and repeated it until it became 'Rama'.
facts: The first shloka is said to have poured out of his grief on seeing a hunter shoot a bird.
Luv and Kush learned to sing the Ramayana from him.
lessons: Ask who will share the results of your actions.
more: Luv and Kush learned the Ramayana from him and sang it in front of Rama.
The shloka metre he first spoke, the anushtubh, became the metre of the epics.
